# Core elevation

The relative sea-level reconstruction is from a ~12-m thick continuous core, GR/19/C1, from the grover site at Twin Cays, Belize. 

```{r level logger and core top verifiying, fig.width=8,fig.height=8}
loadLL = function(LLfile,logger) {
  
  # read .csv file
  LL = readxl::read_xlsx(LLfile,sheet=1)
  
  # add column of logger name for labelling later
  LL = LL %>% mutate(Type=logger) %>%
    
  # smooth LL data (moving average, window size 3; 30min)
 mutate(smoothedWL = movavg(WaterLevel,3,type='s'))  

  
  return(LL)
  
}

# Twin Cayes logger data
TwinCayes = loadLL(LLfile='data/waterloggers/AG_TFY_20464822_Compensated(TWNCY_water).xlsx',
                   logger='Twin Cayes') %>% # manually chop off end and start times
  slice(1:1451)


# load tidal datums, including MSL, from UTide model Carrie Bow Cay
load('data/tides/CBC_UTidedatums.Rdata')

# elevation of GR/19/C1 core top
# reduced level of core top (dumpy survey): 0.835m
# reduced level of logger sensor (dumpy survey): 0.41m (top of logger) - 13.5cm
GR19C1_coretop = 0.835 - (0.41-13.5/100) # relative to level logger sensor

# ortho height of levelogger sensor
llsensorheight_ortho = -0.13813 - 13.5/100 # top of level logger is: -0.13813 (UTM Zone 16, EGM 2008; GNSS survey of TWINBase, then dumpy levelled to level logger). level logger sensor is 13.5cm below top of level logger

# elevation of GR/19/C1 core top in orthometric heights
GR19C1_coretop_ortho = GR19C1_coretop + llsensorheight_ortho

# elevation of GR/19/C1 core top relative to MSL from UTide
GR19C1_coretop_MSL = GR19C1_coretop_ortho - filter(UTide_datums,datum=='MSL')$ortho_level 

# change LL tides to be relative to MSL from UTide
TwinCayes = TwinCayes %>% mutate(WL_msl=smoothedWL+llsensorheight_ortho-filter(UTide_datums,datum=='MSL')$ortho_level)

p1 = ggplot() + 
  geom_path(data=TwinCayes,
            aes(x=Time,
                y=smoothedWL)) +
  geom_hline(aes(yintercept=GR19C1_coretop),color='red') + # core top elevation
  geom_hline(aes(yintercept=filter(UTide_datums,datum=='MSL')$level),color='blue')+ # MSL datum (from CBC tide gauge)
  theme_classic() +
  labs(y='Elevation (m above water logger sensor)')

p2 = ggplot() + 
  geom_path(data=TwinCayes,
            aes(x=Time,
                y=WL_msl)) +
  geom_hline(aes(yintercept=0),color='blue') + # MSL 
  geom_hline(aes(yintercept=GR19C1_coretop_MSL),color='red') + # core top elevation
  theme_classic() +
  labs(y='Elevation (m msl)')

cowplot::plot_grid(p1,p2,nrow=2)
```
# Tidal levels

## Comparison of Twin Cays and Carrie Bow Cay Tides

Portable HOBO water loggers were deployed at Twin Cays and Carrie Bow Cay to determine if the tides at Carrie Bow Cay are representative of that at Twin Cays.

```{r comapre Twin Cays and Carrie Bow Cay tides}

# Twin Cayes 
TwinCayes = loadLL(LLfile='data/waterloggers/AG_TFY_20464822_Compensated(TWNCY_water).xlsx',
                   logger='Twin Cayes') %>% # manually chop off end and start times
  slice(1:1451) 

# Carrie Bow Caye
CarrieBowCayeLL = loadLL(LLfile='data/waterloggers/AG_TFY_20464821_Compensated(CRBCY_water).xlsx',
                       logger='Carrie Bow Caye') %>%
  slice(27:1472)  # manually chop off end and start times

# Slice both to the same overlapping time period
commonstart = max(min(TwinCayes$Time),min(CarrieBowCayeLL$Time))
commonend = min(max(TwinCayes$Time),max(CarrieBowCayeLL$Time))
TwinCayes = TwinCayes %>% filter(Time >= commonstart, Time <= commonend)
CarrieBowCayeLL = CarrieBowCayeLL %>% filter(Time >= commonstart, Time <= commonend)

# shift Carrie Bow Cay to fit Twin Cays (centre on msl over that period)
shift =  mean(CarrieBowCayeLL$smoothedWL) - mean(TwinCayes$smoothedWL)
CarrieBowCayeLL = CarrieBowCayeLL %>% mutate(smoothedWL = smoothedWL-shift)

# plot to visualise
p = ggplot() +
  geom_line(data=TwinCayes,
            aes(x=Time,y=smoothedWL,color=Type),alpha=0.9) +
  geom_line(data=CarrieBowCayeLL,
            aes(x=Time,y=smoothedWL,color=Type),alpha=0.9) +
  theme_classic() +
  scale_color_manual(values=c('#4393c3','#b2182b')) +
  labs(x='Datetime (UTC)', y='Water level (m)')

p

ggsave('figures/tides/Belize LL comparison.pdf',p,height=3,width=8)
```

## Aligning Carrie Bow Cay Tide Gauge data to Twin Cays

The Carrie Bow Cay Tide Gauge data was shifted to align to the Twin Cays water logger data using the OSU tidal predictions as the tide gauge data did not overlap the duration of our water logger deployment.

```{r load data, message=FALSE}

###### LOAD AND CLEAN CBC TIDE GAUGE DATA #####

# query the names of the sheets in the excel file
sheets=as.list(readxl::excel_sheets('data/tides/Tidegauge_CarrieBowCay_Smithsonian.xlsx'))

# function to read data from a given sheet
readTideGauge = function(x){
  data=readxl::read_excel('data/tides/Tidegauge_CarrieBowCay_Smithsonian.xlsx',sheet=x,skip=1)
}

# load all sheets  
CBC_tidegauge = lapply(sheets,FUN=readTideGauge) %>% rbindlist()

# pivot longer 
CBC_tidegauge = pivot_longer(CBC_tidegauge,cols=`prs(m)`:`rad(m)`,names_to='type',values_to='reading',values_drop_na = FALSE)

CBC_tidegauge_radar = filter(CBC_tidegauge,type=='rad(m)')

# remove outliers
CBC_tidegauge_radar = CBC_tidegauge_radar %>% 
  filter(`Time (UTC)`!=ymd_hms("2018-04-29 23:18:00")) %>%
  filter(`Time (UTC)`!=ymd_hms("2016-07-11 20:17:00")) %>%
  filter(`Time (UTC)`!=ymd_hms("2016-07-11 17:45:00")) %>%
  filter(`Time (UTC)`!=ymd_hms("2016-07-11 17:35:00")) %>%
  filter(`Time (UTC)`!=ymd_hms("2016-07-11 17:05:00")) 

# split into groups based on data gaps
group1 = filter(CBC_tidegauge_radar,`Time (UTC)`>=ymd_hms("2018-08-23 18:26:00")) %>% mutate(group=1)
group2 = filter(CBC_tidegauge_radar,`Time (UTC)`>=ymd_hms("2018-04-29 23:13:00"),`Time (UTC)`<=ymd_hms("2018-04-30 20:25:00")) %>% mutate(group=2)
group3 = filter(CBC_tidegauge_radar,`Time (UTC)`<=ymd_hms("2018-04-11 03:44:00"),`Time (UTC)`>=ymd_hms("2017-04-05 20:37:00")) %>% mutate(group=3)
group4 = filter(CBC_tidegauge_radar,`Time (UTC)`<ymd_hms("2017-04-05 20:37:00")) %>% mutate(group=4)

# regroup
CBC_tidegauge_radar = bind_rows(group1,group2,group3,group4)

# smooth data with 30min windows
CBC_tidegauge_radar = CBC_tidegauge_radar %>% mutate(smoothedWL = movavg(reading,30,type='s'))  

###### LOAD OSU PREDICTIONS #####

# load long-term OSU tidal prediction
OSU_CBC_long = read_csv('data/tides/OSU_CarrieBowCay_long.csv',col_names=FALSE)

# make format tidy
OSU_CBC_long = OSU_CBC_long %>% mutate(Time= ymd_hms(paste(OSU_CBC_long$X1,OSU_CBC_long$X2,OSU_CBC_long$X3,OSU_CBC_long$X4,OSU_CBC_long$X5,OSU_CBC_long$X6, sep="-"))) %>% rename(WaterLevel=X7) %>% mutate(site='Carrie Bow Cay (OSU)') %>% mutate(smoothedWL = movavg(WaterLevel,3,type='s'))# smooth predictions(window size: 30 min)


```

```{r adjust CBC tide gauge to Twin Cays}

OSU_CBC_long = OSU_CBC_long %>% mutate(type='OSU') 

CBC_tidegauge_radar = CBC_tidegauge_radar %>% mutate(type='CBC tide gauge (radar)')

# subset OSU predictions to only the time frame of the tide gauge data
OSU_CBC_tgcompare = filter(OSU_CBC_long,
                           Time>=min(CBC_tidegauge_radar$`Time (UTC)`),
                           Time<=max(TwinCayes$Time)) 

# plot before shifting 
p_bef = ggplot() + 
  geom_path(data=CBC_tidegauge_radar,
            aes(x=`Time (UTC)`,
                y=smoothedWL,
                color=type,
                group=group),alpha=0.5) +
  geom_path(data=OSU_CBC_tgcompare,
            aes(x=Time,y=smoothedWL,color=type),alpha=0.3) +
  geom_path(data=TwinCayes,
            aes(x=Time,
                y=smoothedWL,
                color=Type),alpha=0.5) + 
  theme_classic() +
  scale_color_manual(values=c('#92c5de','#fdb863','#5e3c99')) + 
  labs(y='Water level (m)',x='Datetime (UTC)',color='Type') +
  theme(legend.position = 'top')

###### SHIFT OSU TO TWIN CAYS ########

# trim OSU time to fit level logger deployments
OSU_CBC_LLcompare = OSU_CBC_tgcompare %>% filter(Time >= min(TwinCayes$Time), Time <= max(TwinCayes$Time))

# calculate and perform shift
OSUshift = mean(TwinCayes$smoothedWL)-mean(OSU_CBC_LLcompare$smoothedWL)
OSU_CBC_LLcompare = mutate(OSU_CBC_LLcompare,WaterLevel = smoothedWL + OSUshift)
OSU_CBC_tgcompare = mutate(OSU_CBC_tgcompare,WaterLevel = smoothedWL + OSUshift)
OSU_CBC_long = mutate(OSU_CBC_long,WaterLevel = smoothedWL + OSUshift)

###### SHIFT CBC TIDE GAUGE TO OSU ########

# extract OSU predictions when we have tide gauge data
OSU_overlapTG = slice(OSU_CBC_tgcompare,match(CBC_tidegauge_radar$`Time (UTC)`,OSU_CBC_tgcompare$Time))

# split OSU predictions into groups based on data gaps (for plotting so that geom_path doesn't connect)
group1 = filter(OSU_overlapTG,Time>=ymd_hms("2018-08-23 18:26:00")) %>% mutate(group=1)
group2 = filter(OSU_overlapTG,Time>=ymd_hms("2018-04-29 23:13:00"),Time<=ymd_hms("2018-04-30 20:25:00")) %>% mutate(group=2)
group3 = filter(OSU_overlapTG,Time<=ymd_hms("2018-04-11 03:44:00"),Time>=ymd_hms("2017-04-05 20:37:00")) %>% mutate(group=3)
group4 = filter(OSU_overlapTG,Time<ymd_hms("2017-04-05 20:37:00")) %>% mutate(group=4)
OSU_overlapTG = bind_rows(group1,group2,group3,group4)

# calculate and perform shift
TgShift = mean(CBC_tidegauge_radar$smoothedWL)-mean(OSU_overlapTG$WaterLevel)
CBC_tidegauge_radar = mutate(CBC_tidegauge_radar,WaterLevel = smoothedWL-TgShift)

# plot after alignment
p_aft = ggplot() + 
  geom_path(data=OSU_CBC_tgcompare,
            aes(x=Time,y=WaterLevel,color=type),alpha=0.5) +
  geom_path(data=CBC_tidegauge_radar,
            aes(x=`Time (UTC)`,
                y=WaterLevel,
                color=type,
                group=group),alpha=0.3) +
  geom_path(data=TwinCayes,
            aes(x=Time,
                y=smoothedWL,
                color=Type),alpha=0.5) + 
  theme_classic() +
  scale_color_manual(values=c('#92c5de','#fdb863','#5e3c99')) + 
  labs(y='Water level (m above Twin Cays water logger sensor)',x='Datetime (UTC)',color='Type') +
  theme(legend.position = 'top')

p= cowplot::plot_grid(p_bef,p_aft,align='hv',nrow=2)
p

ggsave('figures/tides/CBC_alignedto_TWC_withOSU.pdf',p,height=8,width=8)

# Cut to two years of data for training UTide model
CBC_tidegauge_radar_2016_2017_2018 = filter(CBC_tidegauge_radar,CBC_tidegauge_radar$`Time (UTC)`<ymd('2018/04/29'))

# export tide gauge data for training UTide model
write.csv(CBC_tidegauge_radar_2016_2017_2018,'data/tides/CBC tidegauge cleaned_2016-2018.csv')

# export tide gauge data not used for training UTide model
CBC_tidegauge_radar_2018_2019 = filter(CBC_tidegauge_radar,CBC_tidegauge_radar$`Time (UTC)`>=ymd('2018/04/29'))
write.csv(CBC_tidegauge_radar_2018_2019,'data/tides/CBC tidegauge cleaned_2018-2019.csv')

# exported shifted OSU tide model
write.csv(OSU_CBC_tgcompare,'data/tides/OSU shifted to TWC.csv')
```

## Compare tide models

We then compare the UTide model, OSU tide model and Admiralty TotalTide model against the data. 

```{r load data, warning = FALSE, message=FALSE}

# load UTide model (relative to water logger sensor)
UTide_CBC = read_csv('data/tides/CBC_2016_2018_trained_utc_18Jul23.csv',col_names=FALSE) 
UTide_CBC = UTide_CBC %>% mutate(datetime=make_datetime(X1,X2,X3,X4,X5,X6))

# load ATT model 
ATT = read.csv('data/tides/CBC time series 2015-2019.csv') # load ATT data
ATT = mutate(ATT, datetime = dmy_hm(time), Type = 'ATT Predictions') 
ATT = mutate(ATT,datetime=datetime+hours(6)) # convert time from GMT-6 to GMT+0 (UTC)

# subset UTide predictions to only the time frame of the tide gauge data
UTide_CBC_tgcompare = filter(UTide_CBC,
                           datetime>=min(CBC_tidegauge_radar$`Time (UTC)`),
                           datetime<=max(TwinCayes$Time)) 

# subset ATT predictions to only the time frame of the tide gauge data
ATT_CBC_tgcompare = filter(ATT,
                           datetime>=min(CBC_tidegauge_radar$`Time (UTC)`),
                           datetime<=max(TwinCayes$Time)) 

# shift ATT to same reference frame using OSU
# extract OSU predictions when we have ATT model predictions
OSU_overlap_ATT = filter(OSU_CBC_tgcompare,Time>=min(ATT_CBC_tgcompare$datetime))
OSU_overlap_ATT = filter(OSU_CBC_tgcompare,Time<=max(ATT_CBC_tgcompare$datetime))
# split OSU predictions into groups based on data gaps (for plotting so that geom_path doesn't connect)
group1 = filter(OSU_overlap_ATT,Time>=ymd_hms("2018-08-23 18:26:00")) %>% mutate(group=1)
group2 = filter(OSU_overlap_ATT,Time>=ymd_hms("2018-04-29 23:13:00"),Time<=ymd_hms("2018-04-30 20:25:00")) %>% mutate(group=2)
group3 = filter(OSU_overlap_ATT,Time<=ymd_hms("2018-04-11 03:44:00"),Time>=ymd_hms("2017-04-05 20:37:00")) %>% mutate(group=3)
group4 = filter(OSU_overlap_ATT,Time<ymd_hms("2017-04-05 20:37:00")) %>% mutate(group=4)
OSU_overlap_ATT = bind_rows(group1,group2,group3,group4)
# calculate and perform shift
ATTshift = mean(ATT_CBC_tgcompare$height)-mean(OSU_overlap_ATT$WaterLevel)
ATT_CBC_tgcompare = mutate(ATT_CBC_tgcompare,WaterLevel = height-ATTshift)
  
# add column for legend in plot
OSU_CBC_tgcompare = OSU_CBC_tgcompare %>%  mutate(type='OSU tide model')
UTide_CBC_tgcompare=UTide_CBC_tgcompare%>% mutate(type='UTide model')
CBC_tidegauge_radar = CBC_tidegauge_radar %>%  mutate(type='Carrie Bow Cay tide gauge')
TwinCayes = TwinCayes %>%  mutate(Type='Twin Cayes level logger')
ATT_CBC_tgcompare = ATT_CBC_tgcompare %>% mutate(type='ATT')

# Plot comparison
plota=ggplot() + 
  geom_path(data=CBC_tidegauge_radar,
            aes(x=`Time (UTC)`,
                y=WaterLevel,
                color=type,
                group=group),
            alpha=0.5) +
  geom_path(data=OSU_CBC_tgcompare,
            aes(x=Time,y=WaterLevel,color=type),
            alpha=0.5) +
  geom_path(data=TwinCayes,
            aes(x=Time,
                y=smoothedWL,
                color=Type),
            alpha=0.3) + 
  theme_classic() +
  scale_color_manual(values=c('#fdb863','#92c5de','#5e3c99','#ca0020')) + 
  labs(y='Water level (m above Twin Cays water logger sensor)',x='Datetime (UTC)',color='Type') +
  theme(legend.position='top')

plotb=ggplot() + 
    geom_path(data=CBC_tidegauge_radar,
            aes(x=`Time (UTC)`,
                y=WaterLevel,
                color=type,
                group=group),
            alpha=0.5) +
    geom_path(data=UTide_CBC_tgcompare,
            aes(x=datetime,y=X7,color=type),
            alpha=0.5) +
  geom_path(data=TwinCayes,
            aes(x=Time,
                y=smoothedWL,
                color=Type),
            alpha=0.3) + 
  theme_classic() +
  scale_color_manual(values=c('#fdb863','#5e3c99','#92c5de','#ca0020')) +

  theme(legend.position='top')

plotc=ggplot() + 
    geom_path(data=CBC_tidegauge_radar,
            aes(x=`Time (UTC)`,

  labs(y='Water level (m above Twin Cays water logger sensor)',x='Datetime (UTC)',color='Type') +

plot_OSU_UTide_compare = cowplot::plot_grid(plota,plotb,plotc,

plot_OSU_UTide_compare

# export ATT Tides used for comparison
```

## Tidal range at Twin Cays

```{r tidal range at Twin Cays from UTide model}

# raw UTide datums from matlab output 
UTide_datums=read.csv('data/tides/CBC_semidiurnaldatums_18Jul24.csv')

# ortho height of levelogger sensor
llsensorheight_ortho = -0.13813 - 13.5/100 # top of level logger is: -0.13813 (UTM Zone 16, EGM 2008; GNSS survey of TWINBase, then dumpy levelled to level logger). level logger sensor is 13.5cm below top of level logger

# shift UTide datums to orthometric reference frame
UTide_datums=UTide_datums %>% mutate(ortho_level=level+llsensorheight_ortho)

# save as .Rdata
save(UTide_datums,file='data/tides/CBC_UTidedatums.Rdata')

# tidal range 
tidalrange = filter(UTide_datums,datum=='MHWS')$ortho_level - filter(UTide_datums,datum=='MLWS')$ortho_level

paste('The tidal range based on the UTide model for Twin Cays is',round(tidalrange,digits=2),'m.')
```

# Indicative meaning of peat-forming mangroves

Elevation surveys at each site were done using a digital level to a temporary benchmark. The elevations between sites were related to a common orthometric datum using GNSS measurements of the temporary benchmarks. The elevations were then related to local tidal datums.

```{r indicative meaning of peat-forming mangroves, warning=FALSE, fig.width=9,fig.height=4}

# load modern surveys of peat-forming mangroves (orthometric heights)
modernsurvey = readxl::read_xlsx('data/field_notes/BelizeNotesConsolidated_21Apr21.xlsx',sheet=2,skip=1)
modernsurvey = pivot_longer(modernsurvey,cols=Grover:CookieMonster,names_to='Site',values_to='values')

# load MTL and HAT from UTide model Carrie Bow Cay 
load('data/tides/CBC_UTidedatums.Rdata')

# convert and tidal datums to be relative to MSL by subtracting ortho height of MSL
modernsurvey=modernsurvey %>% mutate(values_MSL=values-filter(UTide_datums,datum=='MSL')$ortho_level)
UTide_datums=UTide_datums %>% mutate(level_MSL=ortho_level-filter(UTide_datums,datum=='MSL')$ortho_level)
write.csv(file='Results/tides/UTide_datums_TwinCays.csv',UTide_datums)

# calculate RWL and IR
modernsurvey = drop_na(modernsurvey) # remove na values MS
hdr_IM = hdrcde::hdr(x=modernsurvey$values_MSL,prob=95)
hdr_IM_lwr=hdr_IM$hdr[,1] # upper limit of 95% HDR
hdr_IM_upr=hdr_IM$hdr[,2] # lower limit of 95% HDR
unforced_RWL=(hdr_IM_upr+hdr_IM_lwr)/2 # RWL
unforced_IR=(hdr_IM_upr-hdr_IM_lwr) # 2 sigma range 

# calculate density for plotting
IM_density = density(
  modernsurvey$values_MSL,
  na.rm = TRUE,
  bw = 0.015
)

IM_density_df = data.frame(
  x = IM_density$x,
  y = IM_density$y / max(IM_density$y)  
)

p_IM_all = ggplot(data=modernsurvey) + 
  # density plot
  geom_density(aes(x=values_MSL,y=..scaled..),alpha=0.7,na.rm=TRUE,bw=0.015) + 
  # Shade indicative meaning
  geom_area(
    data = subset(
      IM_density_df,
      x >= hdr_IM_lwr & x <= hdr_IM_upr
    ),
    aes(x = x, y = y),
    fill = "steelblue",
    alpha = 0.4
  ) +
  # plot tidal datums
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept=filter(UTide_datums,datum=='LAT')$level_MSL),linetype='dashed') +
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept=filter(UTide_datums,datum=='MLWS')$level_MSL),linetype='dashed') +
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept=filter(UTide_datums,datum=='MTL')$level_MSL),linetype='dashed') +
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept=filter(UTide_datums,datum=='HAT')$level_MSL),linetype='dashed') +
  geom_text(aes(x=filter(UTide_datums,datum=='LAT')$level_MSL-0.03,y=1.0,label='LAT')) +
  geom_text(aes(x=filter(UTide_datums,datum=='MLWS')$level_MSL-0.03,y=1.0,label='MLWS')) +
  geom_text(aes(x=filter(UTide_datums,datum=='MTL')$level_MSL-0.03,y=1.0,label='MTL')) +
  geom_text(aes(x=filter(UTide_datums,datum=='HAT')$level_MSL+0.03,y=1.0,label='HAT')) +
  theme_classic() +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette='Paired',direction=1) +
  labs(y='Density',x='Elevation (m msl)')

p_IM_all

ggsave('figures/indicative_meaning/Twin Cays Indicative range density plot.pdf',p_IM_all,height=4,width=7)


paste('The indicative meaning of peat-forming mangroves in our study is',round(unforced_RWL,digits=2),'+/-',round(unforced_IR/2,digits=2),'m msl.')


```

# Decompaction model 

We modelled sediment compaction using the geotechnical model of Brain et al. (2011; 2012). The model uses measured loss-on-ignition and dry bulk density values to estimate mechanical compaction.

```{r load decompaction data}

# load measured loss-on-ignition and dry bulk density data
LOI=readxl::read_xlsx('data/decompaction_modelling/Decompaction_Belizemodern_normal.xlsx',sheet=1)

# load decompaction model results
DryDensity=readxl::read_xlsx('data/decompaction_modelling/Decompaction_Belizemodern_normal.xlsx',sheet=2)
EffStress=readxl::read_xlsx('data/decompaction_modelling/Decompaction_Belizemodern_normal.xlsx',sheet=3)
```

# Variability in radiocarbon dates

```{r function to tidy raw C14 results}

tidyC14results = function(x) {
  
  # load raw C14 results (.xlsx file from lab)
  dates = readxl::read_xlsx(x,sheet=1)
  
  # split conventional age column into two columns:
  # age, sd
  # and specify intcal20 as calibration curve
  # also append 'BETA' in front of lab ID
  dates = dates %>% mutate(age=as.numeric(substr(`CONVENTIONAL AGE`,
                                                        start=1,
                                                        stop=nchar(`CONVENTIONAL AGE`)-10)),
                           sd=as.numeric(substr(`CONVENTIONAL AGE`,
                                                        start=nchar(`CONVENTIONAL AGE`)-5,
                                                        stop=nchar(`CONVENTIONAL AGE`)-3)),
                           curve='intcal20',
                           labID = paste('BETA',`BETA`),
                           `IRMS d13C` = substr(`IRMS d13C`,start=1,stop=5))
  
  # select only relevant columns for Bchron:
  # lab ID, sample ID, age, sd, calibration curve, depth
  dates = dates %>% select(labID,
                           `SUBMITTER NO`,
                           age,
                           sd,
                           curve,
                           `IRMS d13C`)
  
  # remove rows with no conventional age 
  dates = dates %>% filter(age!='NA')
  
  sheet2=readxl::read_xlsx(x,sheet=2)
  
  dates = dates %>% mutate(Depth=sheet2$Depth,
                           Type=sheet2$Type,
                           Thickness=sheet2$Thickness,
                           Pretreatment=sheet2$Pretreatment)
  
  return(dates)
  
}
```

## Fine fraction vs macrofossils 

```{r spread of ages FF vs spread of macros}

set.seed(42)

# function to compute the age spread at a given depth

calcAgeSpread = function(data){
  
  # calibrate ages
  calibrated_dates = with(data, 
                            BchronCalibrate(ages = age,
                                            ageSds = sd,
                                            calCurves = curve,
                                            positions = Depth,
                                            ids = labID)) 
  # save depths for joining to posterior samples later
  depths = data %>% select(c('Depth','labID')) 

  # sample posterior ages
  age_samples = as.data.frame(sampleAges(calibrated_dates))
  age_samples = age_samples %>% pivot_longer(cols=1:ncol(age_samples),names_to='labID',values_to='age')
  
  # add Depth back in
  age_samples = age_samples %>% left_join(depths,by='labID')
  
  # calculate the sd for every depth
  age_samples = age_samples %>% group_by(Depth) %>% summarise(depth_sd = sd(age))

  return(age_samples)
}

# find dates with more than one date per depth
paireddates = dates %>% group_by(Depth) %>% mutate(count=n()) %>% filter(count>1) %>% ungroup()

# calculate age spread for macrofossils and fine fraction samples respectively
paireddates_macros = filter(dates,Type=='macro') %>% group_by(Depth) %>% mutate(count=n()) %>% filter(count>1)
macros_agespread = calcAgeSpread(paireddates_macros)

paireddates_FF = filter(paireddates,Type=='fine fraction') %>% group_by(Depth) %>% mutate(count=n()) %>% filter(count>1)
FF_agespread = calcAgeSpread(paireddates_FF)

# print results
paste('The 2-sigma spread in macrofossil ages at any given depth ranges from',round(min(macros_agespread$depth_sd*2),digits=0),'to',round(max(macros_agespread$depth_sd*2),digits=0),'years.')
paste('The 2-sigma spread in fine fraction ages at any given depth ranges from',round(min(FF_agespread$depth_sd*2),digits=0),'to',round(max(FF_agespread$depth_sd*2),digits=0),'years.')
```

## Bulk uncertainty from paired fine fraction and macrofossil dates

```{r bulk uncertainty using 95HDR on all data}

# Function to normalise ages to the weighted mean age at that depth (i.e. remove age-depth trend)
normaliseAges = function(x){
  
  # find all dates from this depth
  thisdepth = filter(paireddates,Depth==x)
  
  # sample posterior distributions for each sample
  set.seed(42)
  thisdepth_calibrated = with(thisdepth, 
                        BchronCalibrate(ages = age,
                                            ageSds = sd,
                                            calCurves = curve,
                                            positions = Depth,
                                            ids = labID))
  thisdepth_samples = as.data.frame(sampleAges(thisdepth_calibrated))
  
  # calculate weighted mean age for that depth using the posterior samples
  posterior_variances = apply(thisdepth_samples,MARGIN=2,var) # calculate variance for each sample
  weights = 1 / posterior_variances # weights = 1/variance
  weights = weights / sum(weights) # normalise weights to sum to 1
  thisdepth_mean = as.numeric(as.matrix(thisdepth_samples) %*% weights) # matrix multiplication to compute weighted sum 
  thisdepth_mean = mean(thisdepth_mean) # weighted mean as the mean of the weighted sum
  
  # add data type and pretreatment method back
  datatypes = select(thisdepth,c('labID','Type','Pretreatment'))
  thisdepth_calibrated = rbindlist(thisdepth_calibrated,idcol = 'labID') %>% left_join(datatypes,by='labID')
  
  # calculate ages relative to the weighted means of each age
  thisdepth_calibrated = thisdepth_calibrated %>%  mutate(ageGrid_normalised=ageGrid-thisdepth_mean) 
  
 return(thisdepth_calibrated)
  
}

# function to sum age differences across all depths, to derive an overall distribution of the variability in ages
SumProbabilities = function(x){
  
  # define common age grid
  common_agegrid = seq(from=floor(min(x$ageGrid_normalised)),
                       to=ceiling(max(x$ageGrid_normalised)),
                       length.out=2000)
  
  # interpolate each date to the common age grid
  summed_pdf = x %>%
  group_by(labID) %>%
  group_modify(~ {
  interp_dens = approx(
    x = .x$ageGrid_normalised,
    y = .x$densities,
    xout = common_agegrid,rule=1)
  tibble(
    id = rep(.y$labID[1],length(interp_dens$x)),
    ageGrid_normalised = interp_dens$x,
    density = interp_dens$y
  )}) %>% ungroup() %>% filter(!is.na(density))
  
  # sum across all depths for each age grid
  summed_pdf = summed_pdf %>%
  group_by(ageGrid_normalised) %>% 
  summarise(total_density=sum(density, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% ungroup()
  
  # normalise summed densities, so that total density sums to 1
  # The sum of densities multiplied by the age interval should be 1 (i.e. area under the curve is 1)
  # Since common_agegrid has fixed intervals, sum(total_density) * interval_width should be 1.
  # A simpler way therefore is just to just normalize the sum of total_density to 1.
  summed_pdf = summed_pdf %>%
  mutate(normalised_total_density = total_density / sum(total_density))
  
  return(summed_pdf)
}

# dates with more than one date per depth
paireddates = dates %>% group_by(Depth) %>% mutate(count=n()) %>% filter(count>1) %>% ungroup()

# normalise ages to the weighted mean age of that depth
toapply = as.list(unique(paireddates$Depth))
calib_dates_modelled=lapply(toapply,normaliseAges) %>% rbindlist()

# assign Pretreatment factor levels for plotting
calib_dates_modelled$Pretreatment = factor(calib_dates_modelled$Pretreatment, 
                                              levels = c("NA","A", "AAA-BI","AAA-BS","AAA"))


# sum probabilities to derive an overall probability distribution of normalised age differences across all depths
cumsum_normalisedages = SumProbabilities(calib_dates_modelled)

# sample from summed probability distribution of ageGrid_normalised 
# we do not use hdrcde:hdr.den() as that is sensitive to long tails
# instead, we sample from the summed probability distribution to avoid distortion from long tail outlier 
# the sampling would sample the highest probability region more, which is what we want
simulated_sample = sample(cumsum_normalisedages$ageGrid_normalised,
                          size = 10000,replace = TRUE,
                          prob = cumsum_normalisedages$normalised_total_density)

# compute 95% HDR based on the sample
HDR = hdrcde::hdr(simulated_sample,prob = 95)
HDR_2sd = (HDR$hdr[2]-HDR$hdr[1])/2
HDR_mean = (HDR$hdr[2]+HDR$hdr[1])/2

# plot
p_agespread=ggplot() +
  # plot fine fraction dates
  geom_ridgeline(data=filter(calib_dates_modelled,Type=='fine fraction'),
                 aes(x=ageGrid_normalised,
                   y=positions,
                   height=densities*2000,
                   group=labID,
                   fill=Pretreatment),color='transparent',
                 alpha=0.8) +
  # plot macrofossil dates
  geom_ridgeline(data=filter(calib_dates_modelled,Type=='macro'),
                 aes(x=ageGrid_normalised,
                   y=positions,
                   height=densities*2000,
                   group=labID),linewidth=0.3,fill='transparent',color='grey30') +
  # plot bulk uncertainty
  geom_rect(data=data.frame(xmin=HDR_mean-HDR_2sd,
                            xmax=HDR_mean+HDR_2sd,
                            ymin=0,
                            ymax=880),
            aes(xmin=xmin,xmax=xmax,ymin=ymin,ymax=ymax),alpha=0.2,fill='grey70')+
  geom_segment(data=data.frame(y=0,yend=880,x=HDR_mean,xend=HDR_mean),
               aes(y=y,yend=yend,x=x,xend=xend),
               linetype='dashed',color='grey50',alpha=0.5)+
  theme_classic() +
  scale_y_reverse(breaks=c(0,250,500,750),limits=c(880,0)) +
  scale_fill_roma(discrete=TRUE)+
  labs(x='Normalised age difference (yrs)',y='Depth (cm)')

p_inset=ggplot() +
  geom_area(data=cumsum_normalisedages,
               aes(x=ageGrid_normalised,y=normalised_total_density),fill='grey30',alpha=0.2) +
  geom_point(data=data.frame(x=HDR_mean,y=-0.0001),
             aes(x=x,y=y),size=1)+
  geom_segment(data=data.frame(x=HDR_mean-HDR_2sd,
                               xend=HDR_mean+HDR_2sd,
```

# Age-depth model

We run sensitivity tests on the age-depth model, to test the influence of data sampling, data density, and model used (BChron vs rBacon).

## BChron sensitivity test

We test if the kinks in the age-depth model are due to data density, and having repeated ages sampled at a single depth.To do so, we run the age-depth model for 10 random samples of unique depths (one sample per depth), and then systematically leaving out every nth sample (e.g., leave out every 2nd sample, every 3rd sample ... until every 10th sample). We go up till removing every 10th samples as after the 10, the data density plateaus.

### Generate data subsets

We first generate 10 random data subsets, each with just one unique sample per depth. Then for each of the 10 subsets, we thin it by removing every nth sample (e.g., every 2nd sample, every 3rd sample, ...) 

```{r generate data subsets with unique dates per depth and thinned systematically}

# subsample dates removing every nth sample systematically in each successive test set

allsets = data.frame()
set.seed(42)

paireddates = dates %>% group_by(Depth) %>% mutate(count=n()) %>% filter(count>1)
singledates = dates %>% group_by(Depth) %>% mutate(count=n()) %>% filter(count==1)


for (n in 1:10) { # generate 10 test sets; for each test set,
  
  # to store in this test set
  this_set = data.frame() 
  
  for (i in 1:length(unique(paireddates$Depth))) { # at each depth with repeated ages
    
    # find ages in that depth   
    depth_dates = filter(dates,Depth==unique(paireddates$Depth)[i]) %>% mutate(row_within_depth=seq_along(labID))
    # randomly sample one age
    id = sample(depth_dates$row_within_depth,1) 
    depth_unique = slice(depth_dates,id) 
    # append to store with other depths in this test set 
    this_set = bind_rows(this_set, depth_unique)
  }
  
  # add dates where there is only one date per depth 
  this_set = bind_rows(this_set, singledates) %>% mutate(subset = as.factor(n)) %>% arrange(Depth)
  
  # for this complete test set, systematically remove every ath sample, from every 2nd sample ... to every 10th sample
  for (a in 2:10) {
  toremove = seq(from=a,by=a,to=floor(nrow(this_set)/a)*a)
  thinned_dataset=slice(this_set,-toremove)  %>% 
    mutate(removalID=a)
  thinned_dataset = thinned_dataset %>% mutate(runID=paste0('Set',n,'_thinned_',a),
                             samplesize=nrow(thinned_dataset))
  allsets = bind_rows(allsets,thinned_dataset)
  }
  
}

# plot data density with a (every ath sample being removed): to illustrate that sample size plateaus when a~10
ggplot(data=allsets) +
   geom_point(aes(x=removalID,y=samplesize)) +
  theme_classic() +
  labs(x='n', y='Sample size')


p = ggplot() +
  # plot fine fraction dates
  geom_point(data=allsets,
                 aes(x=age,

  theme_classic() +
  scale_x_reverse()+
  scale_y_reverse()+
  facet_wrap(~runID) +

  theme(legend.position = 'bottom') +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 1)) +
  labs(x='Conventional age (yrs)', 'Depth (m)')

p 

ggsave('figures/BChron_agedepth_sensitivity_subsets.pdf',p,height=9,width=13)
```

### Cross validation

We perform cross validation to assess the BChron model performance for each of these subsets. 

```{r BChron cross validation functions}

# function to compute RMSE in any given iteration of k-fold cross validation by comparing residuals between training and test dataset
compareTrainTest = function(training_set,test_set){
  
  # fit age-depth model to training dataset and generate predictions at the depths of the test set
  age_depth = with(training_set,
                 Bchronology(ages = age,
                             ageSds = sd,
                             calCurves = curve,
                             positions = Depth,
                             positionThicknesses = Thickness,
                             ids = labID,
                             predictPositions = test_set$Depth,
                             extractDate = -69))

  # reformat 
  age_depth = summary(age_depth,type="quantiles",prob=c(0.025,0.5,0.975)) %>%
    rename(lwr_2sd=`2.5%`,median=`50%`,upr_2sd=`97.5%`)
  
  # calibrate ages of the test set
  testages = with(test_set,
                  BchronCalibrate(ages = age,
                                  ageSds = sd,
                                  calCurves = curve,
                                  positions = Depth,
                                  ids = labID)) %>% rbindlist(idcol=TRUE)
  # reformat test ages (true)
  testages = testages %>% group_by(positions) %>% summarise(lwr_true=quantile(ageGrid,probs=0.025),
                                                  median_true=quantile(ageGrid,probs=0.5),
                                                  upr_true=quantile(ageGrid,probs=0.975)) %>% rename(Depth=positions)
  
  # calcualte RMSE based on difference of true and predicted ages
  combined = inner_join(testages,age_depth,by='Depth')
  return(combined)
}

# perform K-fold cross validation, in which the data is split into K groups, and RMSE is computed K times, each time using a different test set.
cvFunc = function(x,K) {
  
  set.seed(42)
  
  cat(sprintf("Started cross-validation test %s at %s\n", x, Sys.time()))
  
  # get data subset 
  data=filter(allsets,runID==x)
  
  # split data into K groups
  groups = sample(rep(1:K, length.out = nrow(data))) # randomly shuffles the distribution of data
  data = data %>% mutate(groups = as.factor(groups))
  
  # unique list of the group numbers
  group_numbers = as.matrix(1:K)
  
  # function to compute RMSE for a given test set 
  predictComparison = function(a) {
    # define test set
    test_set = slice(data,which(groups==group_numbers[a])) %>% arrange(Depth)
    # define training set
    training_set = slice(data,which(groups!=group_numbers[a]))%>% arrange(Depth)
    
    # compute train model and predict at the depths of training set
    comparison = compareTrainTest(training_set,test_set)
    return (comparison)
  }
  
  # calculate RMSE for all K iterations of the K-fold cross validation 
  results = apply(group_numbers,MARGIN=1,FUN=predictComparison)%>% rbindlist() %>% arrange(Depth)
  results = results %>% mutate(test_error=sqrt(mean((results$median_true - results$median)^2)),
                               subset=data$subset,
                               runID=data$runID,
                               nfold = K)
  return(results)

}
```

### Run BChron for subsets

```{r sensitivity test BChron unique ages each depth}

toapply=as.list(unique(allsets$runID))

# function to run the sensitivity test
runBChronSensitivitySingleAges = function(x){
  
  # log_file <- sprintf("logs/run_%03d.log", x)
  # sink(log_file, append=TRUE, split=TRUE)
  cat(sprintf("Started run %s at %s\n", x, Sys.time()))
  
  datestorun = filter(allsets,runID==x) 
  
  result = tryCatch(
    withCallingHandlers({
    
  # run age-depth model
  age_depth = with(datestorun,
                 Bchronology(ages = age,
                             ageSds = sd,
                             calCurves = curve,
                             positions = Depth,
                             positionThicknesses = Thickness,
                             ids = labID,
                             predictPositions = PDL$depth*100,
                             extractDate = -69))
  
  # reformat for plotting in ggplot
    age_depth_alldata_bchron = summary(age_depth,type="quantiles",prob=c(0.025,0.5,0.975)) %>%
      rename(lwr_2sd=`2.5%`,median=`50%`,upr_2sd=`97.5%`) %>% 
      mutate(model=as.factor(x),removalID=datestorun$removalID[1],subset=datestorun$subset[1])
    age_depth_alldata_bchron
  }, 
  
  # intercept run if error message is encountered and output warning
  warning = function(w) {
      if (grepl("truncatedWalk.*lower limit higher than upper limit", conditionMessage(w))) {
        message(sprintf("⚠️ Skipping run %s due to truncatedWalk warning", x))
        invokeRestart("muffleWarning")  # prevent warning from propagating
        stop("Invalid prior constraints (truncatedWalk)")  # convert to error so tryCatch handles it
      }
  }),
    
  # output error message if run fails
  error = function(e) {
    message(sprintf("❌ Bchronology failed on run %s: %s", x, e$message))
    return(NULL)
  })
  
  # otherwise output result
  cat(sprintf("Finished run %s at %s\n\n", x, Sys.time()))
  sink()
  return(result)
}
```

# Paleotidal range change

This section of code formats the RSL data to the format needed to extract paleotides from Sulzbach et al. (2023) global paleotidal study. We extract paleotides not just for our core location, but also for all sites within the Belize database.

```{r function to round all ages to nearest 0_5kyrs to extract Sulzbach et al 2023 paleotidal data}

# round ages to nearest 0.5 kyrs as the Sulzbach et al. 2023 dataset outputs paleotidal levels in the Holocene in 0.5 kyrs intervals

roundTime = function(paleotideinput,x){
  
  data=slice(paleotideinput,x)
  timedecimal=data$time - trunc(data$time)
  
  if  ((timedecimal<0.75 & timedecimal>=0.5) | timedecimal<0.25) { # round up to nearest 0.5 
    
    roundedtime = floor(timedecimal*2)/2
    
  } else if ((timedecimal<0.5 & timedecimal>=0.25) | timedecimal>=0.75) { # round down to nearest 0.5
    
    roundedtime = ceiling(timedecimal*2)/2
  }
  
  data = mutate(data, time = trunc(data$time)+roundedtime)
  return(data)
  
}

```

We compare the tidal-range change modelled by two different paleotidal models: Hill et al. (2011) (as in Khan et al., 2017) and Sulzbach et al. (2023).

We applied the paleotidal results of the Sulzbach et al. (2023) model (scaled to present-day tidal datums) as an uncertainty to quantify potential changes in the indicative meaning.

The Sulzbach et al. (2023) model predicts larger tidal range change, especially prior to 8kyrs BP.

```{r format and calculate tidal range change for Khan et al. 2017}

# load data
Khanetal2017_paleotides = readxl::read_xlsx('data/paleotides/Khanetal2017_Paleotides.xlsx',sheet=1) %>%
  filter(year!='0 (OSU)')
Khanetal2017_OSU = readxl::read_xlsx('data/paleotides/Khanetal2017_Paleotides.xlsx',sheet=1) %>% filter(year=='0 (OSU)')

# find percentage change in tidal datums relative to paleotidal model year 0, except for model year 0 where you preserve the original values
Khanetal2017_paleotides = Khanetal2017_paleotides %>% group_by(lat,lon) %>% 
  mutate(across(
    .cols = colnames(Khanetal2017_paleotides)[4:10],
    .fns = function (x) { 
      y0 = x[which(year==0)]
      if_else(year==0,NA,(x-y0)/y0)
      }
    )) %>% ungroup() %>% filter(year!=0)

# scale OSU tidal datums by percentage change 
Khanetal2017_paleotides = bind_rows(Khanetal2017_paleotides,Khanetal2017_OSU) %>% group_by(lat,lon) %>% 
  mutate(across(
    .cols = colnames(Khanetal2017_paleotides)[4:10],
    .fns = function (x) { 
      y_OSU = x[which(year=="0 (OSU)")]
      if_else(year=="0 (OSU)",NA,y_OSU+x*y_OSU)
      }
  )) %>% ungroup() %>% filter(year!="0 (OSU)") %>% mutate(model="Hill et al. (2011)") %>% mutate(year=as.numeric(year))

# calculate tidal range change
Khanetal2017_OSU=mutate(Khanetal2017_OSU,year=0)
Khanetal2017_paleotidalrange_change = bind_rows(Khanetal2017_OSU,Khanetal2017_paleotides)
Khanetal2017_paleotidalrange_change = Khanetal2017_paleotidalrange_change %>% mutate(across(
  .cols = colnames(Khanetal2017_paleotidalrange_change)[4:10],
  .fns = function (x) { 
    y_OSU = x[which(year==0)]
    x - y_OSU
    })) %>% ungroup() %>% filter(year!=0)

# export scaled tidal range change
write.csv(Khanetal2017_paleotidalrange_change,'data/paleotides/Khanetal2017_Paleotides_scaled.csv')

```

```{r format and calculate tidal range change for Sulzbach et al model for this study}

# load Sulzbach et al. 2023 model results for GR/19/C1 and Belize database combined
Sulzbachmodel2023_modelresults_raw = bind_rows(
  mutate(readxl::read_xlsx('data/paleotides/Belize_Paleotide_result_Sulzbachmodel_raw_Howard_20250813.xlsx',sheet=1),time=as.factor('model0')), # Belize database 
  mutate(readxl::read_xlsx('data/paleotides/Belize_Paleotide_result_Sulzbachmodel_raw_Howard_20250813.xlsx',sheet=2),time=as.factor(time)),
  mutate(readxl::read_xlsx('data/paleotides/Belize_Paleotide_result_Sulzbachmodel_raw_Howard_20250807.xlsx',sheet=1),time=as.factor('model0')), # GR/19/C1 
  mutate(readxl::read_xlsx('data/paleotides/Belize_Paleotide_result_Sulzbachmodel_raw_Howard_20250807.xlsx',sheet=2),time=as.factor(time)) # GR/19/C1 
  ) # Belize database 

# load present-day tidal datums
OSU_Belize = read.csv('data/paleotides/Belize OSU tidal datums.csv',skip=1) %>% mutate(model='OSU') # load OSU
load('data/CBC_UTidedatums.Rdata') # load UTide model datums for Twin Cays Sites
UTide_datums = UTide_datums %>% mutate(level_msl = level-filter(UTide_datums,datum=='MSL')$level) %>% select(c('datum','level_msl')) %>% pivot_wider(names_from='datum',values_from='level_msl') # format UTide datums

# replace OSU with UTide model for Twin Cays data
TWC_index = which(OSU_Belize$StudySite=='Twin Cays')
presentdaydatums_Belize = OSU_Belize
for (x in 1:length(colnames(OSU_Belize)[2:8])) {
  col = colnames(OSU_Belize)[2:8][x]
  presentdaydatums_Belize[[col]][TWC_index] = UTide_datums[[col]]
} 
presentdaydatums_Belize[["model"]][TWC_index] = 'UTide'

write.csv(presentdaydatums_Belize,'data/paleotides/presentdaydatums_BelizeDatabse_6Aug2025.csv')

# find fraction change in tidal datums relative to paleotidal model year 0, except for model year 0 where you preserve the original values
Sulzbachmodel_paleotides = Sulzbachmodel2023_modelresults_raw %>% group_by(lat,lon) %>% 
  mutate(across(
    .cols = colnames(Sulzbachmodel2023_modelresults_raw)[5:14],
    .fns = function (x) { 
      y0 = x[which(time=='model0')]
      if_else(time=='model0',NA,(x-y0)/y0)
      }
    )) %>% ungroup() %>% filter(time!='model0') %>% mutate(model='Sulzbach et al. (2023)')

# scale tidal datums by percentage change 
Sulzbachmodel_paleotides = bind_rows(select(Sulzbachmodel_paleotides,                                           
                                            c(colnames(select(presentdaydatums_Belize,-MTL, -StudySite)),'IM')),
                                     select(presentdaydatums_Belize,-MTL,-StudySite)) # combine present-day tides with fraction changes from Sulzbach et al. 2023  model
Sulzbachmodel_paleotides = Sulzbachmodel_paleotides %>% group_by(sampleID) %>% # scale present-day tides by percentage changes 
  mutate(across(
    .cols = colnames(Sulzbachmodel_paleotides)[2:7],
    .fns = function (x) {
      y_presentday = x[which(model!="Sulzbach et al. (2023)")]
      if_else(model=="Sulzbach et al. (2023)",y_presentday+x*y_presentday,NA)
      })) %>% ungroup() %>% filter(model=="Sulzbach et al. (2023)") %>% mutate(model="Sulzbach et al. (2023)")

# add year back in
Sulzbachmodel_paleotides=Sulzbachmodel_paleotides %>% mutate(time=bind_rows(
  readxl::read_xlsx('data/paleotides/Belize_Paleotide_result_Sulzbachmodel_raw_Howard_20250813.xlsx',sheet=2),
  readxl::read_xlsx('data/paleotides/Belize_Paleotide_result_Sulzbachmodel_raw_Howard_20250807.xlsx',sheet=2))$time)

# add scaledwith back in
Sulzbachmodel_paleotides = Sulzbachmodel_paleotides %>% mutate(scaledto = presentdaydatums_Belize$model)

# calculate spring tidal range
Sulzbachmodel_paleotides = Sulzbachmodel_paleotides %>% mutate(range=MHWS-MLWS)

# calculate tidal range change
Sulzbachmodel_paleotides = Sulzbachmodel_paleotides %>% mutate(tidalrangechange=range-(presentdaydatums_Belize$MHWS-presentdaydatums_Belize$MLWS))

# export scaled paleotidal ranges
write.csv(Sulzbachmodel_paleotides,'results/paleotides_Sulzbach2023_BelizeDatabse_6Aug2025.csv')
```

# RSL reconstruction

We calculate the decompacted RSL sequence for the GR/19/C1 core by applying the local indicative meaning and Bchron age model. The compaction was modelled using the geotechnical model of Brain et al. (2011; 2012). We also add additional uncertainty for paleotidal range change, derived by scaling the UTide model datums by the fraction change in tidal datums from the Sulzbach et al. (2023) model.

## GR/19/C1 full age-depth model reconstruction 

```{r calculate RSL}

# load BChron age-depth model results (full dataset)
age_depth_alldata_bchron=read.csv('results/age-depth model outputs/age-depth_alldata_Bchron.csv') %>% rename(depth=Depth) 

# load and calculate paleotidal levels for incorporating paleoindicative range change uncertainty 
paleotides_TWC = read.csv('results/paleotides_Sulzbach2023_BelizeDatabse_6Aug2025.csv') %>% filter(sampleID=='GR/19/C1') %>% mutate(originalRWL=unforced_RWL,originalIR=unforced_IR)
paleotides_TWC = paleotides_TWC %>% mutate(newupper=pmax(HAT,(originalRWL+originalIR/2)),
                                           newlower=pmin(LAT,(originalRWL-originalIR/2))) 
paleotides_TWC = paleotides_TWC %>% mutate(paleotide_corr_RWL=(newupper+newlower)/2,
                                           paleotide_corr_IR=newupper-newlower)

# convert depths to m
RSL=select(age_depth_alldata_bchron,c('depth','lwr_2sd','upr_2sd')) %>% mutate(depth=depth/100,mid_age=(lwr_2sd+upr_2sd)/2) %>% rename(age_lwr_2sd=lwr_2sd,age_upr_2sd=upr_2sd)
  
# calculate sample elevations (to midpoint of sample)
  RSL = mutate(RSL, 
               sample_elev = GR19C1_coretop_MSL - depth,
               RWL=unforced_RWL,
               IR=unforced_IR)
  
  # levelling uncertainty for dumpy: difference between backsites and foresights max. 0.06m
  # levelling uncertainty for GNSS: from GPS report
  # core shortening/stretching uncertainty,
  # non-vertical drilling uncertainty
  # decompaction uncertainty
  RSL = mutate(RSL, 
               IR_uncertainty_2sd = unforced_IR/2, # 2 sigma
               levelling_uncertainty_dumpy = 0.2, # largest uncertainty from dumpy levellling, and also accounts for the fact that GR core was lower (but we know it has to be within tidal range of 0.22m)
               levelling_uncertainty_GPS = 0.04, # largest uncertainty in GNSS measurements
               core_uncertainty_russian = 0.01,
               nonvertical_uncertainty=0.02*depth)
  
  # add decompaction and uncertainty; only includes rows with same depths between decompaction dataset and age-depth model
  RSL = inner_join(RSL,PDL,by='depth')

  # calculate RSL 
  RSL = mutate(RSL, 
               RSL = sample_elev-unforced_RWL+PDL)
  
  # calculate total RSL uncertainty, by adding in quadrature the uncertainty components above
  # non-vertical drilling is a uni-directional uncertainty (can only make things longer, not shorter)
  RSL = mutate(RSL, 
               RSL_uncertainty_up = sqrt(IR_uncertainty_2sd^2+
                                        levelling_uncertainty_dumpy^2+
                                        levelling_uncertainty_GPS^2+
                                        core_uncertainty_russian^2+
                                        nonvertical_uncertainty^2+
                                        (2*`PDL sd`)^2),
               RSL_uncertainty_down = sqrt(IR_uncertainty_2sd^2+
                                        levelling_uncertainty_dumpy^2+
                                        levelling_uncertainty_GPS^2+
                                        core_uncertainty_russian^2+
                                        (2*`PDL sd`)^2))
  
  # format lower and upper bound of RSL
  RSL = mutate(RSL, 
               RSL_lwr_2sd=RSL-RSL_uncertainty_down,
               RSL_upr_2sd=RSL+RSL_uncertainty_up)

# paleo indicative range change uncertainty
RSL = RSL %>% mutate(paleotide_corr_RWL=paleotides_TWC$paleotide_corr_RWL,
                                     paleotide_corr_IR=paleotides_TWC$paleotide_corr_IR)
RSL = RSL %>% mutate(correctedRSL=RSL-(paleotide_corr_RWL-RWL))
RSL = mutate(RSL, 
               corrRSL_uncertainty_up = sqrt((0.5*paleotide_corr_IR)^2+
                                        levelling_uncertainty_dumpy^2+
                                        levelling_uncertainty_GPS^2+
                                        core_uncertainty_russian^2+
                                        nonvertical_uncertainty^2+
                                        (2*`PDL sd`)^2),
               corrRSL_uncertainty_down = sqrt((0.5*paleotide_corr_IR)^2+
                                        levelling_uncertainty_dumpy^2+
                                        levelling_uncertainty_GPS^2+
                                        core_uncertainty_russian^2+
                                        (2*`PDL sd`)^2))
# format lower and upper bound of RSL
RSL = mutate(RSL, 
                       corrRSL_lwr_2sd=correctedRSL-corrRSL_uncertainty_down,
                       corrRSL_upr_2sd=correctedRSL+corrRSL_uncertainty_up)

# remove RSL data associated with depths that are possibly non-mangrove.
RSL = RSL %>% filter(depth<=11.6) # filter ages to depths <= 11.6 m, corresponding to depth before drop in LOI, and depth where mangrove pollen still dominated. The lowest pollen sample at 11.67 m depth contained a lot of non-mangrove pollen, so we know the mangrove ended above 11.67 m depth. Strat observations indicate gradual transition at 11.70 m depth. Geochem supports mangrove existence at and above 11.54 m depth.
```

```{r RSL reconstruction using GR19C1 as SLIPs Response to Reviewer3}
# For purpose of this test we do not use PDL correction and paleotidal range change correction (these are derived at depths of the age-depth model and are small anyway; comparison plot of SLIPs to the original pseudo-SLIPs shows no discernable difference).

                                            positions = Depth,
                                            ids = labID)) %>% rbindlist(idcol=TRUE) %>% rename(labID='.id') %>% group_by(labID) %>% summarise(age_lwr_2sd=quantile(ageGrid,prob=0.025),age_upr_2sd=quantile(ageGrid,prob=0.975)) %>% mutate(age=(age_lwr_2sd+age_upr_2sd)/2)

# add age of core top (2019 CE)
calib_dates_modelled=bind_rows(data.frame(labID='core top',
                                          age_lwr_2sd=-69-1,
                                          age_upr_2sd=-69+1,
                                          age=-69),calib_dates_modelled)

# get age component from radiocarbon dates
RSL = inner_join(calib_dates_modelled,select(dates_cleaned,c('Depth','Thickness','labID')),by='labID') %>% mutate(Depth=Depth/100) %>% # convert depths to m 
rename(depth=Depth)

# calculate sample elevations (to midpoint of sample)
  RSL = mutate(RSL, 
               sample_elev = GR19C1_coretop_MSL - depth,
               RWL=unforced_RWL,
               IR=unforced_IR)
  
  # levelling uncertainty for dumpy: difference between backsites and foresights max. 0.06m
  # levelling uncertainty for GNSS: from GPS report
  # core shortening/stretching uncertainty,
  # non-vertical drilling uncertainty
  # decompaction uncertainty
  RSL = mutate(RSL, 
               IR_uncertainty_2sd = unforced_IR/2, # 2 sigma
               levelling_uncertainty_dumpy = 0.2, # largest uncertainty from dumpy levellling, and also accounts for the fact that GR core was lower (but we know it has to be within tidal range of 0.22m)
               levelling_uncertainty_GPS = 0.04, # largest uncertainty in GNSS measurements
               core_uncertainty_russian = 0.01,
               nonvertical_uncertainty=0.02*depth)
  
  # calculate RSL 
  RSL = mutate(RSL, 
               RSL = sample_elev-unforced_RWL)
  
  # calculate total RSL uncertainty, by adding in quadrature the uncertainty components above
  # non-vertical drilling is a uni-directional uncertainty (can only make things longer, not shorter)
  RSL = mutate(RSL, 
               RSL_uncertainty_up = sqrt(IR_uncertainty_2sd^2+
                                        levelling_uncertainty_dumpy^2+
                                        levelling_uncertainty_GPS^2+
                                        core_uncertainty_russian^2+
                                        nonvertical_uncertainty^2),
               RSL_uncertainty_down = sqrt(IR_uncertainty_2sd^2+
                                        levelling_uncertainty_dumpy^2+
                                        levelling_uncertainty_GPS^2+
                                        core_uncertainty_russian^2))
  
  # format lower and upper bound of RSL
  RSL = mutate(RSL, 
               RSL_lwr_2sd=RSL-RSL_uncertainty_down,
               RSL_upr_2sd=RSL+RSL_uncertainty_up)

# remove RSL data associated with depths that are possibly non-mangrove.
```

## RSL calculations for sensitivity tests

We calculate RSL for different input age-depth models, to assess the sensitivity of the RSL reconstruction to the underlying age-depth model structure. For this sensitivity analysis, we do not include any correction for paleotidal range changes as this correction is time-dependent, and would introduce unequal comparison between different sensitivity runs.

```{r calculate RSL variations for sensitivity test}

################# function to calculate RSL based on an input age-depth model #################

calcGR19C1RSL = function(x) {
  
  # extract age-depth model for this run
  agedepth=filter(BChron_sensitivity_runs_SingleAges_tidy,model==x) %>% filter(depth<=1160)

  # convert depths to m
  RSL=select(agedepth,c('depth','lwr_2sd','upr_2sd')) %>%
    mutate(depth=depth/100,mid_age=(lwr_2sd+upr_2sd)/2) %>% rename(age_lwr_2sd=lwr_2sd,age_upr_2sd=upr_2sd)
  
  # calculate sample elevations (to midpoint of sample)
  RSL = mutate(RSL, 
               sample_elev = GR19C1_coretop_MSL - depth,
               RWL=unforced_RWL,
               IR=unforced_IR)
  
  # levelling uncertainty for dumpy: difference between backsites and foresights max. 0.06m
  # levelling uncertainty for GNSS: from GPS report
  # core shortening/stretching uncertainty,
  # non-vertical drilling uncertainty
  # decompaction uncertainty
  RSL = mutate(RSL, 
               IR_uncertainty_2sd = unforced_IR/2, # 2 sigma
               levelling_uncertainty_dumpy = 0.06,
               levelling_uncertainty_GPS = 0.04,
               core_uncertainty_russian = 0.01,
               nonvertical_uncertainty=0.02*depth)
  
  # add decompaction and uncertainty; only includes rows with same depths between decompaction dataset and age-depth model
  RSL = inner_join(RSL,PDL,by='depth')

  # calculate RSL 
  RSL = mutate(RSL, 
               RSL = sample_elev-unforced_RWL+PDL)
  
  # calculate total RSL uncertainty, by adding in quadrature the uncertainty components above
  # non-vertical drilling is a uni-directional uncertainty (can only make things longer, not shorter)
  RSL = mutate(RSL, 
               RSL_uncertainty_up = sqrt(IR_uncertainty_2sd^2+
                                        levelling_uncertainty_dumpy^2+
                                        levelling_uncertainty_GPS^2+
                                        core_uncertainty_russian^2+
                                        nonvertical_uncertainty^2+
                                        (2*`PDL sd`)^2),
               RSL_uncertainty_down = sqrt(IR_uncertainty_2sd^2+
                                        levelling_uncertainty_dumpy^2+
                                        levelling_uncertainty_GPS^2+
                                        core_uncertainty_russian^2+
                                        (2*`PDL sd`)^2))
  
  # format lower and upper bound of RSL
  RSL = mutate(RSL, 
               RSL_lwr_2sd=RSL-RSL_uncertainty_down,
               RSL_upr_2sd=RSL+RSL_uncertainty_up)
  
  # format lower and upper bound of RSL, and add model ID
  RSL = mutate(RSL, 
               model=unique(agedepth$model),
               removalID=unique(agedepth$removalID))

  return(RSL)
}

############# apply function to calculate RSL based on different age-depth sensitivity runs ############

# load results of age-depth sensitivity analysis 
# (sampled one date per depth, and tested removing every nth sample)
BChron_sensitivity_runs_SingleAges_tidy=read.csv('results/BChron_bootstrap_runs_SingleAges.csv')
BChron_sensitivity_runs_SingleAges_tidy = BChron_sensitivity_runs_SingleAges_tidy %>%
  mutate(removalID= substr(model,
                         nchar(as.character(model))-1,
                         nchar(as.character(model)))) %>% rename(depth=Depth)

# list to apply function to calculate RSL
agedepth_sensitivityruns = as.list(unique(BChron_sensitivity_runs_SingleAges_tidy$model))

# calculate RSL 
RSL_sensitivityruns_singleages=lapply(agedepth_sensitivityruns,calcGR19C1RSL) %>% rbindlist()

# reformat RSL to format for EIV-IGP model, use values corrected for 
RSL_sensitivityruns_EIVIGPinput = data.frame(
  RSL=(RSL_sensitivityruns_singleages$RSL_upr_2sd+RSL_sensitivityruns_singleages$RSL_lwr_2sd)/2,
  RSLer_up_2sd=(RSL_sensitivityruns_singleages$RSL_upr_2sd-RSL_sensitivityruns_singleages$RSL_lwr_2sd)/2, # 2sigma error
  Age=RSL_sensitivityruns_singleages$mid_age,
  Age_up_er_2sd=RSL_sensitivityruns_singleages$age_upr_2sd-RSL_sensitivityruns_singleages$mid_age, # 2sigma error
  RSLError=(RSL_sensitivityruns_singleages$RSL_upr_2sd-RSL_sensitivityruns_singleages$RSL_lwr_2sd)/4, # 1sigma error
  AgeError=(RSL_sensitivityruns_singleages$age_upr_2sd-RSL_sensitivityruns_singleages$mid_age)/2, # 1sigma error
  AgeCE = 1950-RSL_sensitivityruns_singleages$mid_age,# age in CE
  model=RSL_sensitivityruns_singleages$model,
  removalID=RSL_sensitivityruns_singleages$removalID
)

# plot to visualise RSL data in sensitivity runs
ggplot(mapping=aes(xmin=Age-Age_up_er_2sd,
                xmax=Age+Age_up_er_2sd,
                ymin=RSL-RSLer_up_2sd,
                ymax=RSL+RSLer_up_2sd,
                tip1=Age,
                tip2=RSL,
                color=model))+
  geom_rect(data=RSL_sensitivityruns_EIVIGPinput,alpha=0.5,fill=NA,linewidth=0.5) + #color='#92c5de'
  theme_classic() +
  scale_x_reverse() +
  labs(x='Age (yrs BP.)',y='RSL (m)') +
  theme(legend.position = 'nonee')+
  scale_color_batlow(discrete=TRUE)+
  facet_wrap(~removalID)

# export to test stat model sensitivity to underlying age-depth model input
write.csv(RSL_sensitivityruns_EIVIGPinput,'results/GR19C1_RSL_sensitivityruns_EIVIGPinput.csv')
```

```{r temporal model GR/19/C1}
# load our record

# summarise HDR for changepoints and slopes for changepoint model rates
calcHDR = function(cp,beta) {
  cp_hdr = data.frame()
  for (n in 1:ncol(cp)) {
    cp_lwr = 1950-as.numeric(hdrcde::hdr(x=cp[,n],prob=95)$hdr[,1])*1000
    cp_upr = 1950-as.numeric(hdrcde::hdr(x=cp[,n],prob=95)$hdr[,2])*1000
    cp_mid = 0.5*(cp_lwr+cp_upr)
    
    cp_hdr_tobind = data.frame(lwr=cp_lwr,upr=cp_upr,cp_mid,cp=n,model='EIV-CP')
    cp_hdr=bind_rows(cp_hdr,cp_hdr_tobind) 
  }
  beta_hdr = data.frame()
  for (n in 1:ncol(beta)) {
    
    beta_upr = as.numeric(hdrcde::hdr(x=beta[,n],prob=95)$hdr[,1])
    beta_lwr = as.numeric(hdrcde::hdr(x=beta[,n],prob=95)$hdr[,2])
    beta_mid = 0.5*(beta_upr+beta_lwr)
    beta_95err = 0.5*(beta_upr-beta_lwr)
    
    beta_hdr_tobind = data.frame(mid = beta_mid,err95 = beta_95err,beta=n,model='EIV-CP')
    beta_hdr = bind_rows(beta_hdr,beta_hdr_tobind)
  }
  return(list(cp_hdr,beta_hdr))
}

  scale_color_hawaii(discrete=TRUE) + 
  scale_fill_hawaii(discrete = TRUE) +
  labs(x="Age (BP)",y="Rate (mm/yr)") 

p = cowplot::plot_grid(p_est,p_rates,align='hv',nrow=2)
p

ggsave('Figures/GR19C1 temporal models.pdf',p,height=7,width=7)

paste('The EIV-IGP model predicts RSL fluctuations that peak at ~7.6, 7.0 and 5.4 kyrs BP.')

```

```{r maximum rate in GR/19/C1 core including sensitivity tests}

# load nseg setting sensitivity tests
load('results/EIV-IGP model outputs/GR19C1_test_nseg.Rdata')

# load age-depth input sensitivity tests 
load('results/EIV-IGP model outputs/GR19C1_NIspline_nseg14_sensitivityruns.Rdata')

# load NIspline model results for GR19C1
GR19C1_NIspline = read.csv('results/ReSLR NIspline model outputs/GR19C1 NIspline model nseg14.csv') %>% mutate(model='NI spline')

# load EIV-IGP model results for GR19C1
GR19C1_EIVIGP = read.csv('results/EIV-IGP model outputs/GR19C1_EIVIGP_defaultsettings.csv') %>% mutate(model='EIV-IGP')

# combine all rates
GR19C1_rate_ensemble = bind_rows(
  mutate(select(GR19C1_EIVIGP,c(Age_BP,rate_pred:rate_lwr)),model='EIVIGP GR/19/C1'),
  mutate(select(GR19C1_NIspline,c(Age_BP,rate_pred:rate_lwr)),model='NIspline GR/19/C1'),
  mutate(select(GR19C1_test_nseg,c(Age_BP,rate_pred:rate_lwr)),model='NIspline nseg test'),
  mutate(select(GR19C1_NIspline_sensitivityruns,c(Age_BP,rate_pred:rate_lwr)),model='NIspline age-depth test'))

# filter to 8.1 kyrs BP to present
GR19C1_rate_ensemble = filter(GR19C1_rate_ensemble,Age_BP<=8100)

# calculate max and min rates across ensemble
maxrate=filter(GR19C1_rate_ensemble,rate_pred==max(GR19C1_rate_ensemble$rate_pred))  %>% mutate(meanrate=0.5*(rate_upr+rate_lwr),rate_err=0.5*(rate_lwr-rate_upr))

minrate = filter(GR19C1_rate_ensemble,rate_pred==min(GR19C1_rate_ensemble$rate_pred)) %>% mutate(meanrate=0.5*(rate_upr+rate_lwr),rate_err=0.5*(rate_lwr-rate_upr))

# Print manuscript text
paste('The rates of RSL rise modelled for the GR/19/C1 core never exceeded',round(maxrate$meanrate,digits=1),'+/-',round(maxrate$rate_err,digits=1),'mm/yr (2 sigma).')

paste('The minimum rates of RSL rise modelled for the GR/19/C1 core was',round(minrate$meanrate,digits=1),'+/-',round(minrate$rate_err,digits=1),'mm/yr (2 sigma).')

# Manuscript text for EIV-IGP rate at 7.6 kyrs BP
rate_7_6ka_EIVIGP = GR19C1_EIVIGP %>% filter(Age_BP==7596.0125) %>%
  mutate(meanrate=0.5*(rate_upr+rate_lwr),rate_err=0.5*(rate_lwr-rate_upr))
paste('The RSL rate at 7.6 ka based on the EIV-IGP model is', 
round(rate_7_6ka_EIVIGP$meanrate,digits=1), '+/-', round(rate_7_6ka_EIVIGP$rate_err,digits=1),
'mm/yr (2 sigma).')

# Manuscript text for maximum rate at 7.6 kyrs BP in the GR/19/C1 core
GR19C1_rate_ensemble_7_6ka = GR19C1_rate_ensemble %>% 
  mutate(yearBP_approx=round(Age_BP/1000,digits=1)) %>% filter(yearBP_approx==7.6)

maxrate_7_6ka=filter(GR19C1_rate_ensemble_7_6ka,
                     rate_pred==max(GR19C1_rate_ensemble_7_6ka$rate_pred)) %>%
  mutate(meanrate=0.5*(rate_upr+rate_lwr),rate_err=0.5*(rate_lwr-rate_upr))

paste('The maximum RSL rate at 7.6 ka was', 
round(maxrate_7_6ka$meanrate,digits=1), '+/-', round(maxrate_7_6ka$rate_err,digits=1),
'mm/yr (2 sigma) across all sensitivity runs of the GR/19/C1 core.')
```

### Test effect of priors on EIV-IGP model

To address Simon's comment, we compare the following runs of the EIV-IGP model:
- EIV-IGP model from reslr package (default settings; used in manuscript)
- EIV-IGP model from Cahill et al 2015 (default settings)
- EIV-IGP model from Cahill et al 2015 (originally published prior settings: prior rate centered at 4 mm/yr)
- EIV-IGP model from Cahill et al 2015 with prior rate centred at 40mm/yr rate but small variance (sigma.g ~ dgamma(80,2))
- EIV-IGP model from Cahill et al 2015 with prior rate centred at 40mm/yr rate but large variance (sigma.g ~ dgamma(20,0.5))

```{r compare EIVIGP models of different prior settings}

# load GR19C1
GR19C1 = read.csv('results/SLIPs/RSLallages_Bchron_EIVIGPinput.csv')

# load results from the models

##  load results from reslr package
EIVIGP_reslr =  read.csv('results/EIV-IGP model outputs/GR19C1_EIVIGP_defaultsettings.csv') %>% mutate(model='reslr') %>% mutate(model=factor(model,levels=c('reslr','EIVIGPdefault','EIVIGP_Cahill2015priors','EIVIGP_TestPrior_G80_2','EIVIGP_TestPrior_G20_0-5')))

## load results from Niamh's model
filelist=as.list(list.files('results/EIV-IGP model outputs/GR19C1_EIVIGP_Cahillmodel_testpriors'))
read_EIVIGPresults = function(x){
  filename = substr(x,29,nchar(x))
  filepath = paste0('results/EIV-IGP model outputs/GR19C1_EIVIGP_Cahillmodel_testpriors/',x)
  RSL = read.csv(paste0(filepath,'/RSL_Estimates.csv'))
  rate = read.csv(paste0(filepath,'/RSL_Rates.csv'))
  result = right_join(RSL,rate,by='year') %>% mutate(model=filename) %>% rename(Age_BP=year)
  return(result)
}
EIVIGP_runs = lapply(filelist,read_EIVIGPresults) %>% rbindlist() %>% 
  mutate(model=factor(model,levels=c('reslr','EIVIGPdefault','EIVIGP_Cahill2015priors','EIVIGP_TestPrior_G80_2','EIVIGP_TestPrior_G20_0-5')))

# plot
p_est = ggplot() +
  # plot our record
  geom_rect(data=GR19C1,aes(xmin=Age-Age_up_er_2sd,
                xmax=Age+Age_up_er_2sd,
                ymin=RSL-RSLer_up_2sd,
                ymax=RSL+RSLer_up_2sd),alpha=0.1,fill=NA,linewidth=0.3,color='grey80') +
  # plot Cahill2015 model EIV-IGP runs
  geom_path(data=EIVIGP_runs,aes(x=Age_BP,y=SL_est,color=model)) +
  geom_ribbon(data=EIVIGP_runs,aes(x=Age_BP,ymin=SL_lwr,ymax=SL_upr,fill=model),alpha=0.35)+
  # plot reslr EIV-IGP
  geom_path(data=EIVIGP_reslr,aes(x=Age_BP,y=pred,color=model),linetype='dashed',linewidth=0.4) +
  geom_path(data=EIVIGP_reslr,aes(x=Age_BP,y=lwr,color=model),linetype='dashed',linewidth=0.4) +
  geom_path(data=EIVIGP_reslr,aes(x=Age_BP,y=upr,color=model),linetype='dashed',linewidth=0.4) +
  theme_classic() +
  scale_x_reverse() +
  scale_color_manual(values=c("#1B9E77", "#D95F02", "#7570B3", "#E7298A",'black')) +
  scale_fill_manual(values=c("#1B9E77", "#D95F02", "#7570B3", "#E7298A"))+
  labs(x='Age (BP)',y='RSL (m))')

p_rate = ggplot() +
  # plot Cahill2015 model EIV-IGP runs
  geom_path(data=EIVIGP_runs,aes(x=Age_BP,y=rate_est,color=model)) +
  geom_ribbon(data=EIVIGP_runs,aes(x=Age_BP,ymin=rate_lwr,ymax=rate_upr,fill=model),alpha=0.35)+
  # plot reslr EIV-IGP
  geom_path(data=EIVIGP_reslr,aes(x=Age_BP,y=rate_pred,color=model),linetype='dashed',linewidth=0.4) +
  geom_path(data=EIVIGP_reslr,aes(x=Age_BP,y=rate_lwr,color=model),linetype='dashed',linewidth=0.4) +
  geom_path(data=EIVIGP_reslr,aes(x=Age_BP,y=rate_upr,color=model),linetype='dashed',linewidth=0.4) +
  theme_classic() +
  scale_x_reverse() +
  scale_color_manual(values=c("#1B9E77", "#D95F02", "#7570B3", "#E7298A",'black')) +
  scale_fill_manual(values=c("#1B9E77", "#D95F02", "#7570B3", "#E7298A"))+
  labs(x='Age (BP)',y='RSL rate (mm/yr)') 

p = cowplot::plot_grid(p_est,p_rate,align='hv',nrow=2)
p

ggsave('figures/compare_EIVIGP_priors.pdf',p,height=6,width=8)
```

```{r message=FALSE}
# Interpolate GIA models to time points of GR/19/C1 reconstruction
toapply=as.list(unique(GIA_TWC$model))
calcGIAmisfit=function(x){
  GIA = filter(GIA_TWC,model==x)
  GIA = approx(x=GIA$age,y=GIA$RSL,xout=-GR19C1$Age/1000)
  misfit = GIA$y-GR19C1$RSL # positive means overpredict, negative means underpredict
  misfit = data.frame(age_kyrBP=-round(GIA$x,digits=1),misfit_m=misfit,model=x)
  return(misfit)
}
GIAMisfits = lapply(toapply,FUN=calcGIAmisfit) %>% rbindlist()

GIAMisfits_mean=GIAMisfits %>% group_by(model, age_kyrBP) %>% summarise(mean_misfit=round(mean(misfit_m),digits=1)) %>% ungroup()
```

```{r GIA Belize database comparison, warning=FALSE}
# load GIA results

# functions to tidy GIA results
reformatGIA = function(data, site){
  subset=slice(data,seq(from=site*27+1,by=1,to=(site+1)*27))
  GIA = slice(subset,3:27) %>% rename(ageBP=Time.kaBP.,
                                      RSL=RSL,
                                      RSL_lwr_2sd=RSL.2sigma,
                                      RSL_upr_2sd=RSL.2sigma.1)
  GIA = GIA %>% mutate(RSL=as.numeric(RSL),
                       RSL_lwr_2sd=as.numeric(RSL_lwr_2sd),
                       RSL_upr_2sd=as.numeric(RSL_upr_2sd))
  GIA = GIA %>% mutate(site=subset[1,1],lat=subset[1,3],lon=subset[1,2]) %>% mutate(ageBP=-(as.numeric(ageBP)))
  return(GIA)
}
tidyGIAensemble = function(data){
  GIA = lapply(sites,function(site) reformatGIA(data,site)) %>% rbindlist()
}

# apply functions to tidy GIA results

GIA_Belize_ANU = tidyGIAensemble(GIA_Belize_ANU) %>% mutate(model='ANU-ICE')

# tidy for plotting
scale=1

SLIPs= filter(BelizeDatabase,Type==0)
SLIPs$upper = SLIPs$RSL + SLIPs$RSL_up_er_2sd # ymax value
SLIPs$lower = SLIPs$RSL - SLIPs$RSL_low_er_2sd # ymin value
SLIPs$left = SLIPs$Age - SLIPs$Age_low_er_2sd  # xmin value
SLIPs$right = SLIPs$Age + SLIPs$Age_up_er_2sd # xmax value

marL=filter(BelizeDatabase,Type==-1)
marL$upper = marL$RSL - marL$RSL_low_er_2sd # y value of horizontal line
marL$lower = marL$upper - scale # y value for bottom of tick mark
marL$xmid = marL$Age
marL$left = marL$Age-marL$Age_low_er_2sd # xmin value
marL$right = marL$Age+marL$Age_up_er_2sd # xmax value

terrL=filter(BelizeDatabase,Type==1)
terrL$lower = terrL$RSL + terrL$RSL_up_er_2sd # y value of horizontal line
terrL$upper = terrL$lower + scale # y value for bottom of tick mark
terrL$xmid = terrL$Age
terrL$left = terrL$Age-terrL$Age_low_er_2sd # xmin value
terrL$right = terrL$Age+terrL$Age_up_er_2sd # xmax value
```

```{r load EST-GP model results}

# load RSL and rate outputs
ESTGP_RSL=read.csv('results/Erica STeHM/Belize_TwoComponents/RSL.csv')
ESTGP_Rates = read.csv('results/Erica STeHM/Belize_TwoComponents/RSLrates.csv')

ESTGP_Rates_global_samples = read.csv('results/Erica STeHM/Belize_TwoComponents/GlobalRates_samples.csv')

# cut to time span of Belize SLIPs
BelizeSLIPs = readxl::read_xlsx('data/BelizeDatabase_6Aug2025.xlsx') %>% mutate(Tectonic=as.factor(Tectonic),Quality=as.factor(Quality)) %>% filter(Type==0)
ESTGP_RSL = filter(ESTGP_RSL,yearBP <= max(BelizeSLIPs$Age))
ESTGP_Rates = filter(ESTGP_Rates,yearBP <= max(BelizeSLIPs$Age))
ESTGP_RSL_global_samples = filter(ESTGP_RSL_global_samples, yearBP <= max(BelizeSLIPs$Age)) 
ESTGP_Rates_global_samples = filter(ESTGP_Rates_global_samples, yearBP <= max(BelizeSLIPs$Age))

# print max global RSL
minESTGP_RSL_global = ESTGP_RSL %>% filter(component==2 & model_ranking==0) %>% 
  filter(RSL==min(RSL))
paste('The maximum RSL from the global component is',round(minESTGP_RSL_global$RSL/1000,digits=0),'+/-',
      round(minESTGP_RSL_global$RSLsd/1000,digits=0),'m at',
      round(minESTGP_RSL_global$yearBP/1000,digits=0),'kyrs BP.')
```

We categorised the 1-52 different model iterations as "optimal", "non-optimal", and "chosen". 
- Optimal: based on mode of histogram of log_p values
- Chosen: the one model from the optimal model subset, which has the highest log_p value
- Non-optimal: all remaining models 

Most optimal models come back similar as the chosen model, and the non-optimal models show very different RSL and rates.

We compare the global RSL component (which accounts for the primary regional trend, mostly from GIA), against GIA models (Figure 3 of manuscript).

To account for model structural uncertainty, we simulate 1000 samples of the global RSL component across all optimal models, then derived summary statistics across the optimal model ensemble. We exclude the non-optimal models as the results are non-intuitive. 

```{r visualise EST-GP global RSL and rate samples}

p1 = ggplot(data=filter(ESTGP_RSL_global_samples,model_ranking!=2)) +
  geom_density_ridges_gradient(aes(x=RSL/1000,y=yearBP,group=yearBP,fill = ..x..),
                               scale=3,rel_min_height=0.01,alpha=0.5) + 
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "C") +
  scale_y_reverse()+
  theme_classic() +
  labs(x='RSL (m)',y="Year (BP)") +
  coord_flip()

p2 = ggplot(data=filter(ESTGP_Rates_global_samples,model_ranking!=2)) +
  geom_density_ridges_gradient(aes(x=rate,y=yearBP,group=yearBP,fill = ..x..),
                               scale=3,rel_min_height=0.01,alpha=0.5) + 
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept=8),linetype='dashed')+
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "C") +
  scale_y_reverse()+
  scale_x_continuous(limits=c(-10,25))+
  theme_classic() +
  labs(x='RSL rate (mm/yr)',y="Year (BP)") +
  coord_flip()

cowplot::plot_grid(p1,p2,nrow=2,align='hv')

# for manuscript text
optimalensemblelength = length(unique(filter(ESTGP_RSL_global_samples,model_ranking!=2)$modelID))
paste('The ensemble results summarises the predicted samples from',optimalensemblelength,'models.')
```

As the RSL distributions appear skewed in the earlier part of the record, we tested the influence of two different summary methods: 

1. 95% Highest Density Region
2. Quantiles (this assumes the data follows a normal distribution)

We find the summary results are similar regardless of the method used.

```{r compare global ESTGP optimal ensemble summary methods}

ESTGP_RSL_global_samples_summary = ESTGP_RSL_global_samples %>% filter(model_ranking!=2) %>% group_by(yearBP) %>% 
  summarise(median=median(RSL)/1000,
            upr=max(hdrcde::hdr(RSL,prob=95)$hdr)/1000,
            lwr=min(hdrcde::hdr(RSL,prob=95)$hdr)/1000) %>% mutate(summary_method='95% HDR')

ESTGP_Rates_global_samples_summary = ESTGP_Rates_global_samples  %>% filter(model_ranking!=2) %>% group_by(yearBP) %>%
  summarise(median=median(rate),
            upr=max(hdrcde::hdr(rate,prob=95)$hdr),
            lwr=min(hdrcde::hdr(rate,prob=95)$hdr)) %>% mutate(summary_method='95% HDR')

  geom_ribbon(data=ESTGP_RSL_global_samples_summary,

  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "C") +

  coord_flip() +

p2 = ggplot() +
```

We stick to using the 95% HDR to be theoretically more accurate as the data does not strictly follow a normal distribution.

The optimal model ensemble summary is very similar to the chosen model.
